x: Alan Bishop finished 15th in the S.L.H.'30' on August 31st, clocking a best ever 3:27:10. Wally Wortley was 24th in 3:39:41. John Moore had a fine run in the Southall '10' on September 7th finishing 3th in 54:12.
Norman Stairs & Wally Wortley carried our colours thro' South London at the head of the field, but the latter soon eased leaving Norman a minute clear at Croydon.

In the Exeter to Plymouth 44 miles road race on May 9th,Alan Bishop(5:52:3) finished 4th and Wally Wortley(6:27:26) was 7th. Wally led at 5 miles but was overtaken by our own Norman Stairs who went way ahead to lead by 3½ minutes at'20'.
Yet again Wally Wortley and Alan Bishop made up the Belgrave team,which was the second English club to close in. Norman Stairs breaks away in the London-Brighton Run.

John Hilton finished in his best time to date in front of Charlie Walker and Pete Sadler who were well up at one point but fell away towards the end Reg Hopkins and Wally Wortley completed our ten finishers.
Duncan and King endorsed their placings in the Bath/Weston race and George Beecham was close behind. It was interesting to see Wally Wortley in competition again.

The veterans of Belgrave, well versed in the ways of the Brighton road, stand quietly out of the way of brasher newcomers with less experience and more to say;John Keown and John Morris are joined this year by John Johnson and Wally Wortley.
Wally Wortley, 10th, led the Bels home with Mac 16th, George Chantler 17th and Arthur Whitehead 21st. Mac's training was a five times a week affair.
From the start our new member Wally Wortley ran extremely strongly and in finishing so high up in such a distinguished field put up a really remarkable show.
